That midday bullish candle, with the upper wick almost as long as the real body.

One guy bought SOL at 87.21.

He said he saw in the group that there was a major positive catalyst, and he was afraid he wouldn’t get on the train.

When he charged in, he even sent a line: “This wave is solid.”

Now the price is back at 85.88, and he’s down nearly two percentage points.

Actually, that move in the morning was pretty fierce—going straight up from 76.92 to gain 11 points.

The problem is volume.

Today’s trading volume is 383 million, which sounds like a lot, but it’s still below the 20-day average volume.

After a move like this, if volume can’t keep up, it’s like someone shouting loudly but not taking a step forward.

Even the RSI is 72.6, sitting in the overbought zone.

The MACD is still in a bearish alignment, with DIF only at 1.91.

The Bollinger Bands are hovering near the midline; the band width is 18.6%, and the direction basically hasn’t been decided.

The guy asked me whether he should add to his position.

I told him, first look at that upper wick before talking.

On the tip of the parabolic curve, there’s never a shortage of people standing guard—an up-thrust with shrinking volume is basically handing the people inside an exit door.

As for the news… by the time you see it, the price has already finished moving.

What’s left is all just a bag-holder relay race.

He didn’t reply for half a day, and in the end he said: “I’ll go place a stop-loss order.”

That upper wick—enough to give anyone who chased higher a dose of trouble.

#BTC #ETH #交易心态 #合约 # risk control

What’s going on
The International Energy Agency (IEA) has made its latest comments: the Iran war is disrupting global energy supply and has caused a “top-level” impact on the oil market. In plain terms, Iran is a core OPEC oil-producing country, and the Strait of Hormuz is the transportation bottleneck for roughly 20% of the world’s crude oil. Once supply is obstructed, oil prices surge → global inflation expectations rise → the Fed is forced to keep high interest rates for longer. The transmission chain is clear: energy crises push up prices → delay rate-cut expectations → tighten liquidity → high-beta risk assets like crypto are the first to be dumped.

Market impact
- Short term: Geopolitical risk-off sentiment heats up. The longer the conflict drags on, the harder diplomatic resolution becomes, and the harder it is for risk appetite to recover.

IEA官方定性：伊朗冲突对全球油市构成史上最大级别冲击，能源危机直接威胁全球经济稳定。

怎么回事
国际能源署（IEA）最新表态，伊朗战争正在扰乱全球能源供应，对石油市场造成“最大级别”的影响。说白了，伊朗是OPEC核心产油国，霍尔木兹海峡更是全球约20%原油的运输咽喉，一旦供应受阻，油价飙升 → 全球通胀预期抬头 → 美联储被迫维持高利率更久。传导链条很清晰：能源危机推高物价 → 降息预期推迟 → 流动性收紧 → 加密这类高贝塔风险资产第一个被抛。

一句话翻译：油价是通胀的导火索，通胀是降息的拦路虎，降息是牛市的发动机——链条断在第一环。

对市场的影响
- 短期：地缘避险情绪升温，BTC现报$69,627.98，24h涨幅8.32%看似强势，但这类地缘冲突初期往往是“先冲高后回落”的剧本，避险资金部分流向黄金和美元。ETH报$2,252.64（24h +17.82%），反弹越猛，地缘利空下的回吐风险越大。

title: BTC一夜拉回6.9万！美联储会议纪要都挡不住这波逼空鹰派纪要+地缘危机双重压制，比特币却在暴力拉升——市场正在讲一个全新的故事
subTitle:
一、先说盘面：BTC暴力反弹，ETH狂飙
北京时间今日凌晨，加密市场走出了一波让很多人措手不及的行情：
BTC 涨至 69,400美元 以上，过去24小时涨幅 7.41%，时隔近三个月重返6.9万美元关口ETH 涨至 2,259美元，过去24小时涨幅高达 18.06%，表现远超BTC过去1小时全网爆仓扩大至 13亿美元，空头被全面碾压
这波行情最令人意外的地方在于——多头是在利空围剿之下打赢的。

二、利空一：美联储会议纪要比想象中更鹰
昨晚公布的美联储7月会议纪要，整体基调是偏鹰的：
3名官员在7月FOMC会议上投票支持加息25个基点，分别是Hammack、Kashkari和Logan多名官员当时已准备支持加息，更多人认为若通胀不降，未来仍需收紧政策整份纪要中没有出现任何支持降息的讨论美联储主席沃什还提出将FOMC会议从每年8次缩减至6次
按常理，这种鹰派纪要应该打压风险资产。但BTC用7%的涨幅回应了这份文件——市场的定价逻辑，正在脱离传统的“政策信号→BTC跟跌”模式。
三、利空二：中东局势仍在恶化
另一个宏观变量来自地缘政治：
特朗普加入以色列对伊朗的战争，霍尔木兹海峡石油天然气运输仍然受限，价格压力持续累积布伦特原油已连续多日上涨，通胀预期还在升温
但即便在这个背景下，BTC依然走出了独立的逼空行情，说明短期主导BTC价格的是衍生品市场的清算结构，而非传统宏观逻辑。

四、为什么利空压不住BTC？——逼空的力量
这波上涨最核心的驱动力，是空头被“拉爆”了。
多个来源指出，BTC在纪要公布后的表现说明了一个关键事实：目前加密货币市场的逼空行情和监管利好预期，明显压过了这份偏鹰纪要带来的压力。
同时，有几点值得留意：
BTC现货ETF结束连续多日流出，迎来明显净流入，机构资金给币价下方带来了支撑虽然纪要本身理论上偏空风险资产，但美国财政部扩大长期美债回购，已把30年期收益率明显压了下来，市场没有单纯围着FOMC纪要交易
五、当前关键位置

六、帮你划重点

ETH比BTC猛是一个值得持续观察的信号——如果资金持续从BTC流向主流山寨，市场风险偏好在回升；如果只是单日补涨，则要留意是否只是短期轮动。
最后一句：利空出尽，空头被清算。6.9万之前是天花板，现在可能是地板。但地板是真是假，要看接下来两天的回踩确认。别在人家拉完之后追，等一个回踩确认，比追高舒服一百倍。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Deeply Revisit $DUSK —at the time, I’d already let go of the “1 billion tokens capped” setting. The only hardcore question that really needs to be dissected now is: in this economic operating mechanism, who exactly is paying for those hefty interest rates?

When you break down the underlying design of @Dusk_Foundation , the main drains are basically Gas and Staking. The trouble is that the pitfalls are buried right here. According to the latest official roadmap: the initial issuance is 500 million tokens, and the remaining ~500 million are reserved with a 36-year vesting schedule as node rewards. We’re currently in the first phase, with 19.86 DUSK produced per block. Do the math per day—that’s like shoving nearly 170,000 new chips into the market every day.

Go digging into the real figures from the on-chain explorer, and the mismatch is painfully stark. Over the past 24 hours, total network interaction volume fluctuated around just a couple hundred transactions (with records even as low as 174). Total accumulated transaction fees for the whole day were only a meager 3.3 DUSK. The absurd comparison is that over 200 million tokens are just sitting in contracts earning yield, with an APR still hanging around 22%.

This is the supply-demand gap that’s most worrying: real deployed applications are like a rusted small pipe, while the inflation incentives are an out-of-control giant fire hydrant. Chasing high-interest to accumulate holdings can indeed build a security moat, but if those profits aren’t coming from genuine business revenue—if they’re simply being filled by mindless token minting—then the essence is mortgaging future liquidity. People may covet paper wealth, but I’m wary of the sell-pressure of these tens of thousands of tokens every day. In the end, will there be external capital to pick up the slack?

Recently, @Dusk_Foundation  has been pushing private placements, SME financing, and the RWA track repeatedly. The direction is not bad, and the official has also clearly stated that tokenizing assets doesn’t automatically come with built-in buy demand.

So don’t worry about whatever good news the project team keeps putting out. Just lock onto one metric next: once these so-called old-money assets go live, how much real daily active usage can they actually generate, and how much Gas will they truly consume. If the growth rate of real business is always left behind by the token-minting machine, then even the most “perfect value capture” will eventually turn into nothing more than an unpayable IOU. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Regarding $DUSK, I’ve long since grown numb to that “10 billion coins capped” setup. All that keeps running through my mind is a single soul-searching question: under the current economic structure, who exactly is footing the bill for those high staking interest rates?

If you carefully break down the plan for @Dusk_Foundation , the core purpose of $DUSK  is basically to serve as Gas fees and to lock tokens in nodes. The awkward crux is right here. According to the roadmap provided by the official team, in the early stage 500 million coins will be in circulation, and the remaining 500 million will be gradually released as network rewards over the next 36 years. We’re currently in the first phase, where each block produces about 19.86 DUSK. Assuming more than 8,600 blocks per day, the daily newly added sell-pressure tokens can jump to 170,000 coins.

Now compare that with the real active usage on the mainnet—the data is simply not impressive. Browse the explorer: in the past day, there were only a little over 200 transfers in total (and the recorded figure is even worse, at just 174). The total fees burned across the whole network in a day are only 3.3 DUSK. But the contrast is stark: now more than 200 million tokens are queuing to be locked, and the annualized rate (APR) is still consistently sitting at 22%. In plain terms, it’s “waterfall-like emissions, drip-like consumption.”

High node staking rates can certainly make the chain more resilient under load. But if all of that 22% interest is being paid by essentially minting money out of thin air—not by relying on real on-chain revenue to sustain it—then it’s like using up future capacity in advance. People may look at the interest figures on paper and feel good. But what I’m more concerned about is whether there’s truly real off-chain capital waiting to pick up the bill at the end of the day.

Recently I saw stories about @Dusk_Foundation  starting to frequently onboard SMEs for financing, private placements, and RWA on-chain initiatives. The overall direction is fine. The official team themselves also admit that simply chopping up traditional assets can’t conjure trading depth out of nowhere. So going forward, don’t worry about what partnership press releases the project team puts out. The only thing we should focus on is, after these new businesses land, how many real transfers they can drive and how much DUSK they can burn continuously. If the consumption generated by real-world applications never catches up with the token’s issuance pace, then the so-called value capture will, in the end, just be wishful thinking to fill hunger. #eth $ETH

After Missile Alerts, the UAE Fully Cuts Off Economic and Trade Financial Ties with Iran

Tensions in the Middle East’s geo-political landscape have continued to spill over into the commercial and financial sphere. According to publicly reported accounts, shortly after the UAE issued missile threat alerts from Dubai, it announced it would halt all trade and financial transactions with Iran, putting Iran at risk of losing a critical economic and trade corridor. The move comes amid prolonged regional conflict and increased U.S. pressure on Iran, and it also signals that Gulf states are shifting from largely rhetorical bargaining over strategy toward more tangible economic constraints.

On key facts, the UAE’s defense department said that two ballistic missiles launched from Iran and aimed at maritime traffic triggered alerts. Iran denied responsibility and rejected the related allegations. Hours later, the UAE’s diplomatic authorities said it had stopped all trade and financial dealings with Iran. The statement did not directly name the missile incident, but emphasized that an “escalatory act that undermines regional and global peace and security” prompted its decision, while reaffirming its commitment to dialogue, cooperation, and regional integration. Analysts note that in recent years the UAE has been a major financial and commercial hub for Iran and a key trading partner, with import volumes in the tens of billions of dollars. Observers also suggest that a substantial portion of Iran’s imported goods are routed through the UAE, with Dubai playing a central role in cargo distribution and cross-border capital arrangements.

In terms of impact pathways, this decision’s effects are not limited to “doing one less deal.” For Iran—long subject to high-intensity external sanctions and with restricted links to the international banking system—transshipment, settlement, and corporate networks in a nearby financial and commercial center are often more relevant to day-to-day operations than more distant sanctions provisions. Consulting sources in Tehran point out that Iranian businesses have built extensive commercial connections in the UAE over decades, so the UAE’s trade and financial embargo could, in practical terms, be more direct and more disruptive than some traditional Western sanctions. At the same time, reports say the U.S. is increasingly focusing on economic squeeze measures and continues to restrict operations at Iranian Gulf ports; with disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s external economic loop is already under strain. Tightening the UAE channel effectively adds another blocked “relief valve” on top of existing pressures. What needs to be distinguished is this: the competing claims about missile responsibility cannot yet be settled based on unilateral statements alone; and it is also unclear how much of the actual trade stock remains continuing after the escalation of the conflict. Equating an announcement to “full decoupling” with “economic shutdown immediately” is an overreach.

As for how it may affect the crypto market, the transmission is mostly indirect rather than a single switch for either bullish or bearish sentiment. First, when the risk premium for the Middle East rises, markets often price in energy supply and shipping uncertainty first, and then feed that into volatility and liquidity preferences for global risk assets. Crypto assets—typically a high-volatility risk segment—often absorb sentiment shocks in parallel. Second, when traditional trade settlement and cross-border financial channels tighten, the market will re-evaluate the need for alternative value-transfer tools. However, this is structural speculation, not the same as assuming that short-term funds will necessarily flow into a particular type of token. It also cannot ignore the possibility that compliance and enforcement environments tighten at the same time. Third, if other Gulf countries continue to watch rather than follow suit, the shock may be concentrated—at least temporarily—in Iran’s external economic loop and the regional safe-haven risk premium. Once a chain of restrictions emerges, the narrative could shift from bilateral frictions to a broader geopolitical-financial partition, making correlation trading in crypto markets more sensitive. All of the above are scenario-based projections, not verified causal conclusions.

The editorial assessment is: the UAE’s stance this time indicates that, after its security red lines were crossed, it is willing to transform long-standing ambiguous trade and commercial advantages into a concretely enforceable tool of economic pressure. For Iran, it is “a neighboring-country valve tightening outside of sanctions.” Going forward, three points should be closely monitored: the thickness of enforcement of the ban (whether goods, financial activity, and corporate networks are truly cleared out), whether other Gulf states follow suit, and whether both sides return to cooling-down communications. For observers of the crypto industry, rather than chasing emotion-driven headlines, it may be better to track whether regional risk premiums, stablecoin settlement discussions, and changes in compliance boundaries are heating up in tandem. At the factual level, official economic and trade financial exchanges have been halted. At the effect level—how markets map that to crypto—remains to be validated, so it is not advisable to jump to extreme conclusions in one step.

content:
导弹警报后阿联酋全面中断对伊经贸金融往来

中东地缘紧张持续外溢至经贸层面。据公开报道，阿联酋方面在迪拜发出导弹威胁警报后不久，宣布停止与伊朗的全部贸易及金融交易，使伊朗面临失去一条关键经贸通道的风险。此举发生在地区冲突延宕、美国加大对伊经济施压的背景下，也让海湾国家对伊朗的策略从口头博弈更多转向实质性经济限制。

核心事实方面，阿联酋国防部门称，有两枚自伊朗方向发射、针对海上交通的弹道导弹触发警报；伊朗方面否认对此负责，并驳斥相关指控。数小时后，阿联酋外交部门表态已停止与伊朗的所有贸易和金融往来。声明未直接点名导弹事件，但强调“破坏地区和世界和平与安全的升级行为”促使其作出决定，同时重申致力于对话、合作与区域一体化。分析指出，阿联酋近年是伊朗重要的金融与商业中心和主要贸易伙伴，进口规模达数十亿美元量级；亦有观察称，伊朗相当比例进口物资经阿联酋转口，迪拜在货物集散与跨境资金安排中扮演枢纽角色。

逻辑拆解上看，这一决定的冲击路径并不只在于“少做一笔生意”。对长期处于高强度外部制裁、与国际银行体系联系受限的伊朗而言，邻近金融商业中心的转口、结算与企业网络，往往比远距离制裁条款更具日常运转意义。德黑兰方面咨询人士指出，伊朗企业数十年来在阿联酋积累了广泛商业联系，因此阿联酋侧贸易与金融禁运在实际效果上，可能比部分传统西方制裁更直接、更具破坏性。与此同时，美国据报正把重点更多转向经济挤压，并持续限制伊朗海湾港口运转，叠加霍尔木兹海峡航运受扰，伊朗外部循环本已承压；阿联酋通道收紧，相当于在既有压力之上再堵一条缓冲阀门。需要区分的是：导弹责任归属双方说法对立，尚不能仅凭单方表述定论；贸易实际存量在冲突升级后已有多少仍在继续，公开信息亦不完全清晰。把“宣布脱钩”直接等同于“经济立刻停摆”，属于过度外推。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多是间接传导而非单一利好或利空开关。其一，中东风险溢价抬升时，市场常先交易能源供应与航运不确定性，再映射到全球风险资产的波动率与流动性偏好，加密资产作为高波动风险板块，往往同步承受情绪冲击。其二，当传统贸易结算与跨境金融通道收紧时，市场会重新讨论替代性价值转移工具的需求，但这属于结构性猜想，不等同于短期资金必然流入某类代币，更不能忽视合规与执法环境同步趋严的可能。其三，若海湾其他国家继续观望而非跟进，冲击可能阶段性集中在伊朗外部循环与区域避险溢价；一旦出现连锁限制，叙事会从双边摩擦升级为更广的地缘金融分割，加密市场的相关性交易会更敏感。以上均为路径推演，并非已验证的因果结论。

编辑判断是：阿联酋此次表态，标志着其在安全底线被触碰后，愿意把长期暧昧的经贸便利转化为可兑现的经济压力工具，对伊朗而言是“制裁之外的邻国阀门”收紧。后续应重点观察三点：禁令执行厚度（货物、金融、企业网络是否真正出清）、其他海湾国家是否跟进，以及双方是否重新回到降温沟通。对加密行业观察者而言，与其追逐情绪化标题，不如跟踪区域风险溢价、稳定币结算讨论和合规边界变化是否同步升温。事实层是官方经贸金融往来被叫停；效果层与市场映射仍待验证，不宜一步跳到极端结论。

#termmax @termmax @TermMax This fancy marketing is really something—it's got retail users’ psychology nailed. They’ve set up multiple point systems like XP, AP, and MP, stuffing everything—daily check-ins, water-posting, borrowing (Borrow), and earning (Earn)—into the Puzzle Challenge. If you complete it, you get double rewards. To drive traffic even harder, they even offer a 10x AP bonus for Alpha trading, and their dual-currency earning plans hand out a crazy 60x AP per day. This kind of “baby-sitting” step-by-step guide means nobody has to think; you just follow the instructions and click like crazy. With the countdown to the August 25 TGE already ringing, the market-wide FOMO has been thoroughly ignited.

But behind these shiny numbers, what I see instead is a huge cause for concern. Take a look at the official stats released: the number of registered addresses has broken 1.5 million, daily active users have surged to 90,000, and the on-paper TVL has skyrocketed to 90 million USD. However, when you squeeze the data on DefiLlama a bit, the actual presented TVL is only around 32.5 million USD. The real active lending is roughly 22 million USD. I know different teams may use different calculation models, but with this gap of tens of millions, it’s hard not to dig deeper: among the traffic that was forcibly pulled in by those point-farming sugarbaits and token-issuance expectations, how much of it actually converts into loyal users who are truly willing to leave capital parked long-term?

Anyone who’s been around these circles knows it: logging in every day and doing tasks is, to put it bluntly, just “farming rewards.” At best, it proves that your airdrop bait is enticing enough—but it definitely doesn’t reflect how strong the protocol’s product capabilities really are. Once the August 25 TGE actually lands and $TermMax flows into the market, expectations will be fully maxed out. By then, what will keep these people’s chips from leaving? You can’t keep bluffing with “please stay tuned for the next round of point activities,” right? So, whether tokens will be issued or not is meaningless at this point—the real question is whether this business logic can keep running.

In the end, August 25 is basically a make-or-break threshold. If the lending scale doesn’t suddenly collapse, if trading activity remains strong, and if the funds in the Vault treasury can keep climbing steadily upward, then I’ll admit this money-burning marketing campaign is extremely successful at market education. How the K-line moves on TGE day is just short-term—what determines how long this whole thing can last is how many real people you can keep.#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax @TermMax 这波花式营销确实把散户的心理拿捏得死死的。他们搞出的 XP、AP、MP 几套积分体系，把签到、水帖、借贷（Borrow）和理财（Earn）统统塞进了 Puzzle Challenge，拼凑完整就能拿到双倍奖励。为了刺激流量，甚至给 Alpha 交易开出了 10 倍 AP，双币理财直接给到夸张的每天 60 倍 AP。这种保姆级的操作指南，让大伙儿根本不用费脑子，照着指引一路狂点就行。眼看 8 月 25 日 TGE 的倒计时敲响，整个市场的 FOMO 情绪已经被彻底点燃。

但在这些光鲜亮丽的数字背后，我看到的反而是巨大的隐忧。看看官方放出的战绩：注册地址突破 150 万、日活冲上 9 万、账面 TVL 更是飙到了 9000 万美元。然而，打开 DefiLlama 挤一挤水分，实际呈现的 TVL 也就 3250 万美元上下，真实的活跃贷款大约在 2200 万美元。我知道各家的计算模型有差别，但这几千万美元的缺口摆在这里，难免让人想刨根问底：那些被积分大饼和发币预期强行拽进来的流量里，究竟有几成转化为了真正愿意长期沉淀资金的忠实用户？

常混圈子的都明白，天天打卡做任务，说白了就是在“撸毛”。这顶多能证明你家的空投诱饵放得够香，绝对代表不了协议本身的产品力有多强。等到 8 月 25 日 TGE 落地，$TermMax 正式流向市场，大家的预期也就彻底打满了。到了那个节骨眼上，能留住这批人的筹码是什么？总不能继续忽悠说“敬请期待下一期积分活动”吧。所以，现在讨论会不会发币无意义，核心在于这套业务逻辑还能不能继续运转。

说到底，8 月 25 日就是个见光死的门槛。如果平台的借贷规模没有雪崩，交易活跃度依然坚挺，Vault 金库里的资金还能稳步向上，那我绝对承认这波烧钱营销是极其成功的市场教育。TGE 当天的 K 线怎么走都是短期的，能留下多少活人，才是决定这个盘子能活多久的关键。#eth $ETH

Recently watching @TermMax, I find myself increasingly thinking that what it most needs to prove right now isn’t whether there’s “enough cooperation,” but whether these collaborations have truly turned into its own ecosystem.

Morpho, Aave, Venus, Pendle—plus Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Berachain, HyperEVM, Robinhood Chain… the list is indeed impressive. The official data disclosed recently is also strong: TVL exceeding $90 million, over 1.5 million registered wallets, and coverage of 10 EVM chains. The problem is that when I look at third-party data, I notice something quite striking: DefiLlama’s TermMax TVL is only about $32.5 million, and one Ethereum chain alone accounts for roughly 95%.

I understand that different parties may use different counting methodologies, but from an ecosystem perspective, this gap is still worth asking about: as for the so-called “multi-chain ecosystem,” has there already formed real cross-chain capital demand, or is it mostly still staying at the deployment and partnership level? If more than 90% of the funds ultimately get squeezed into Ethereum, then how much incremental assets, new users, and liquidity other chains truly bring matters more than simply “how many chains have been integrated.”

Recently, Binance Wallet also added a Booster to TermMax, directly putting $2 million worth of $TMX into the campaign—so naturally the hype will rise. But a large number of the tasks are still things like following, reposting, joining Discord, connecting a wallet, and making posts. That can quickly expand reach, but what I want to see more is what happens after the campaign ends: how many of these people will actually go on to do fixed-rate borrowing, provide liquidity, or even stay long-term? #BTC 

The TGE on August 25 is already very close. For @TermMax, the next stage’s truly convincing metrics shouldn’t be about “who has been partnered with” anymore—it should be about how much capital and real usage have been retained after the collaborations.

Otherwise, as the ecosystem roster keeps getting longer while the funds remain concentrated in one place, there’s still plenty of room to question this “ecosystem prosperity.” #ETH

Over the past few days, I’ve really been going through TermMax. My biggest takeaway isn’t that it’s “hard to use”—it’s that it keeps trying to hide complex things, but it hasn’t hidden them completely.

After the V2 launch at the end of May, @termmax  stuffed the multi-chain market, limit orders, positions, and historical records into a single interface. It even stresses that “users shouldn’t do the protocol’s work for it.” I agree with the direction. The problem is that where ordinary people really get stuck isn’t that they need to switch chains less—it’s that they don’t even know what they’ve bought in the first place.

You have to understand FT, XT, and GT: check the maturity date, distinguish fixed-income returns from leveraged returns, and keep an eye on LTV, liquidation lines, and authorization limits. Even in the official tutorials, users have to set the ERC-20 spending cap themselves—and it even says “users can exit anytime.” Exiting early doesn’t mean it all just goes back to the original price with one button. Fundamentally, you still need to see whether there’s a counterparty in the market, the current quote, and the slippage. For experienced DeFi users, this isn’t a big deal. But for people encountering fixed-rate products for the first time, a nice-looking APY on the page doesn’t mean they truly understand what risks they’re taking on.

What I care about more is what to do if things go wrong. If authorization fails, is it because the limit is too low or because of a wallet issue? If the quote suddenly changes, is it due to insufficient depth or a change in the term? If the position is close to liquidation, should the user only see an LTV number—or should it directly tell them: “If it drops by how much, you’ll run into trouble; and if you add how much collateral, you’ll return to the safe zone”? These details are what truly determine whether ordinary people dare to use it long-term.

And not to mention that on August 25, TMX will be having its TGE. Attention will quickly shift from “is the product good to use?” to “how much is the points worth, and how do I open the tokens.” At that moment, I actually want to ask even more: after V2 implements unified routing and a one-screen position view, shouldn’t the next step be to explain the risks within that same screen too? Don’t make users flip through documentation to learn by themselves. #ETH 

TermMax’s product logic isn’t really bad. What I question is this: a protocol that focuses on fixed rates and tries to make DeFi feel more like a financial product still ends up defaulting to users becoming half a protocol researcher first. Has that barrier really come down?

#TermMax  $BTC  @termmax

Japan reduced its holdings of U.S. Treasuries for the second consecutive month, yet remains the top overseas holder

Data released by the U.S. Department of the Treasury on international capital flows show that in June 2026, major economies made clear adjustments to their holdings of U.S. Treasuries. As the largest overseas holder of U.S. Treasuries, Japan cut about $26.4 billion in that month, bringing its holdings down to about $1.12 trillion; the size of the reduction ranked first among the major holders. Reports from outlets such as Nikkei Chinese also noted that Japan has been trimming its U.S. Treasuries for two straight months. In the same period, total U.S. Treasury holdings by foreign investors decreased by about $72.1 billion month-over-month, with the total falling to about $9.3 trillion. Among the past four months, declines occurred in three.

From a structural perspective, the reductions among the top overseas holders are not isolated. China cut about $25.9 billion in the same month, with its holdings falling to about $633.4 billion; the UK reduced by about $8.7 billion, with holdings around $939.9 billion. Cayman Islands, France, Luxembourg, and others also saw declines to varying degrees, while Canada and Belgium recorded increases. Overall foreign holdings retreated, largely driven by large-scale selling by major holders such as Japan and China. The figures above reflect changes in stock as of the end of June. They are disclosures made after the fact under official reporting standards and do not directly equate to a month’s on-the-spot, trade-by-trade mapping of selling activity.

Logically, the market has linked Japan’s latest round of selling to movements in the yen and the backdrop of intervention in FX markets. In recent months, the yen has faced persistent downward pressure. The Tokyo side reportedly took intervention measures to stabilize the exchange rate, and market participants have also asked whether the U.S. may have been involved in related actions. Some observers had previously worried that, to secure the U.S. dollar liquidity needed for intervention, Japan’s authorities or related accounts might sell U.S. Treasuries, thereby affecting, at the margin, the supply-demand balance for U.S. Treasuries and the U.S.’s long-term borrowing costs. It is important to emphasize: a decline in holdings can be caused by a combination of factors, such as maturities not being reinvested, valuation effects and account adjustments, and rebalancing of reserve management. The media and market interpretation of “selling to defend the yen” is a background-based inference, not a single causal explanation directly proven step-by-step by Treasury reports. The fact that the UK and China adjusted in parallel also suggests that June’s foreign investor behavior is not governed by a single narrative.

For the crypto market, it is more prudent to focus on transmission paths rather than tagging short-term sentiment. One path is the supply-demand and yield expectations for U.S. Treasuries: if major overseas holders continue to reduce duration or scale, it could lift the central expectation for Treasury yields, which would then, through real-rate dynamics and dollar liquidity conditions, affect the global pricing environment for risk assets. Crypto assets, as high-volatility, risk-on instruments, are often more sensitive to real rates and how tight or loose dollar liquidity is. A second path is signals from reserve and official-sector fund reallocation: when large official holders adjust the composition of their dollar assets, the market will reassess the relative attractiveness of dollar assets, which can in turn influence how funds are split across asset classes such as equities, credit, gold, and digital assets. A third path is risk premia and cross-asset linkage: if volatility in U.S. Treasuries rises, global volatility and demand for safe havens may move in tandem. The crypto market could face pressure both from liquidity tightening, or—at certain stages—from absorbing hedging and diversification demand; the direction is not automatically one-way.

In the editor’s view, the key is to understand the June data as a “disclosure of the results of official holdings rebalancing,” rather than as real-time trading instructions. Japan still maintains its position as the largest overseas holder. A single-month change of $26.4 billion is not a structural reversal relative to its stock of about $1.12 trillion. What truly needs ongoing monitoring is whether, over the following months, a trend of sustained selling develops; whether U.S. long-end yields subsequently show persistent supply-related premia; and how yen policy and the interest-rate spread between the U.S. and Japan evolve. For participants in the crypto market, the focus should not be to sensationalize one-off holdings data. Instead, it should be to assess whether such data indirectly strengthens constraints related to real interest rates, dollar liquidity, and risk appetite. If subsequent data show that foreign holdings stabilize and long-end supply pressure eases, the tightening narrative above could weaken. If selling continues in step with rising yields, then the discounting and leverage environment for risk assets may still be constrained. The facts have become relatively clear, but the path outlook still depends on verifying subsequent developments in interest rates, exchange rates, and official-sector fund flows.

content:
日本连续两月减持美债持仓仍居海外首位

美国财政部公布的国际资本流动相关数据显示，2026年6月主要经济体对美国国债的持仓出现明显调整。作为美债最大的海外持有国，日本当月减持约264亿美元，持仓规模降至约1.12万亿美元，减持幅度在主要持有方中居首。日经中文网等报道亦指出，日本已连续两个月减持美债。同期，外国投资者整体持有的美国国债环比减少约721亿美元，总额降至约9.3万亿美元，过去四个月中有三个月出现下降。

从结构看，前几大海外持有方中减持并不孤立。中国当月减持约259亿美元，持仓降至约6334亿美元；英国减持约87亿美元，持仓约9399亿美元。开曼群岛、法国、卢森堡等亦有不同程度下降，而加拿大、比利时等则录得增持。整体外资持仓回落，主要受到日本与中国等大规模减持的影响。上述数据反映的是截至6月底的存量变化，属于官方统计口径下的事后披露，并不直接等同于当月即期市场抛售节奏的逐笔映射。

逻辑上，市场将本轮日本减持与日元走势及汇市干预背景联系在一起。近几个月日元持续承压，东京方面曾采取干预以稳定汇率，外界亦关注美方是否参与相关行动。部分观察人士此前担忧，为筹措干预所需美元流动性，日本官方或相关账户可能出售美债，从而在边际上影响美债供需与美方中长期借贷成本。需要强调的是：持仓下降可由到期未续作、估值与账户调整、储备管理再平衡等多种因素共同形成，媒体与市场解读中的“为捍卫日元而抛售”属于基于背景的推断，并非财政部报表逐条证明的单一因果。英国、中国等同步调整，也说明6月外资行为并不只有单一叙事。

对加密市场而言，更宜关注传导路径而非短期情绪标签。路径之一是美债供需与收益率预期：若主要海外持有方持续降低久期或规模，可能抬升美债利率中枢预期，从而通过实际利率与美元流动性条件，影响全球风险资产的定价环境；加密资产作为高波动风险偏好品种，往往对实际利率与美元松紧更为敏感。路径之二是储备与官方资金的再配置信号：当大型官方持有人调整美元资产结构时，市场会重新评估美元资产的相对吸引力，进而影响跨资产资金在股票、信用、黄金与数字资产之间的切分。路径之三是风险溢价与联动：若美债波动上升，全球波动率与避险需求可能同步变化，加密市场既可能因流动性收紧承压，也可能在部分阶段承接对冲与分散化需求，方向并不自动单向。

编辑观察认为，当前更应把6月数据理解为“官方持仓再平衡的结果披露”，而不是实时交易指令。日本仍保持最大海外持有国地位，单月264亿美元的变化相对其约1.12万亿美元存量并非结构性翻盘；真正需要持续跟踪的，是后续数月是否形成趋势性减持、美债长端利率是否因此出现持续的供给溢价，以及日元政策与美日利率差如何演化。对加密市场参与者，重点不在于把单次持仓数据情绪化，而在于评估其对实际利率、美元流动性与风险偏好的间接约束是否加强。若后续数据显示外资持仓趋稳、长端供给压力缓和，则上述紧缩叙事可能减弱；若减持与收益率上行同步延续，则风险资产的折现与杠杆环境仍可能受到压制。事实层已相对清晰，路径推演仍取决于后续利率、汇率与官方资金流动的验证。

title: ETH 暴涨：牛市启动，还是一场巨型逼空？
subTitle:
$ETH 
{spot}(ETHUSDT)
 这两天的走势非常有意思。
价格从 $2,000 附近快速拉升到 $2,200–$2,300 区域，短时间涨幅非常惊人。
但我觉得，现在最值得关注的不是“ETH 涨了多少”，而是：
这轮上涨到底是谁在买？
我把目前的几个信号放在一起看，答案可能没有那么简单👇
① 第一股力量：宏观环境突然改善
美国财政部宣布，将部分长期国债回购规模从此前的 $2B 提高到至少 $4B/次。
消息出来后，美债长端收益率明显回落，美元也走弱，风险资产整体获得提振。
这给 BTC 和 ETH 的上涨提供了一个非常重要的宏观催化剂。
但要注意：
Treasury buyback 更像是点火器，而不是 ETH 上涨的全部燃料。

② 第二股力量：空头被连续挤压
这可能是这轮 ETH 加速上涨最容易被忽略的因素。
8 月 19 日，加密市场出现约 $1.44B 的空头清算。
更夸张的是，Hyperliquid 上一个 50,000 ETH 的空头仓位，在大约 12 秒内被强平，单笔损失约 $24M。
这就是典型的：
价格上涨 → 空头止损/爆仓 → 被迫买入 → 价格继续上涨 → 更多空头爆仓。
也就是 Short Squeeze。
所以 ETH 现在的涨幅里，肯定有一部分来自“被迫买盘”。

③ 但这并不意味着上涨是假的
这里才是我认为真正重要的地方。
ETH ETF 的资金流已经出现改善。
8 月 18 日，美国现货 ETH ETF 净流入约 $71.5M。
换句话说：
这不是纯粹的合约市场自嗨。

宏观催化

风险偏好回升

现货/ETF资金改善

ETH 突破关键位置

空头集中平仓

进一步推高 ETH

现在 ETH 已经来到一个非常关键的区域：
$2,300–$2,500
这个区域过去就是比较明显的供应/阻力区域。
所以我不会因为 ETH 暴涨就直接喊“下一站 $3,000”。
我的判断反而是：
$2,300 = 第一关
$2,500 = 趋势确认关
如果 ETH 能够放量突破 $2,500，并且回踩后继续站稳，那么这轮行情就有机会从：
“逼空反弹”
逐渐转变成：
“现货资金推动的趋势行情”。

空头已经被清得差不多了，接下来谁来接盘？
这可能就是短线最大的风险。

🟢 宏观环境：偏利好

#ETH  Has the bull market arrived? No! Don’t go all-in, and don’t chase the rally.

The surge is brutal. In a pure crypto market, major coins that break out of consolidation trigger a violent rally, igniting widespread frenzy. People think the bull is here—and it seems it might still climb. But once the market reaches the tail end—when it comes to Ethereum, the question is whether it can even touch 2400 again—no matter whether it does or doesn’t, both futures contracts and spot should avoid chasing during this kind of heated moment.

Frenzy means getting trapped one after another, followed by regret. For futures, it’s often in the “top sprint” phase and then a choppy range afterwards. For spot, it’s “up and keep selling”—this refers to major coins like Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Is the market truly on its way to a bull market from here? I don’t think so. This could be the last rebound within a bear market. If Ethereum can’t hold above 2400 and keep rising without turning back, then the real bull hasn’t arrived. The market will likely enter a deeper pullback phase too. If Ethereum revisits 1500, whether it can break below 1500—both depend on whether the bottom is solid. $ETH  is currently a sell zone. If you sell now, you sell more as it rises.
{spot}(ETHUSDT)
This time, Bitcoin hasn’t been as strong as Ethereum. It’s unlikely to reach 82000. $BTC —going to 71000–74500 as the extreme?

For spot, I don’t advocate rushing to buy right away. There will be good opportunities in September and October.
{spot}(BTCUSDT)
Are you regretting now that you didn’t buy Bitcoin around 60000—right on the dot? You hesitated too much?

There will still be chances in September and October. When the time comes, don’t keep hesitating. My strategy then: start daily DCA around 60000, and place batch buy limit orders in stages below—every 2400 USD—with accumulating orders.

This is the most painful stage at the end of the bear market. Don’t rush. After these last couple of months pass, the larger-scale upward move will come.

｜Why is ETH up 18% today? Three reasons—the last one you might not have noticed
$ETH is up 17.4% today, jumping from 1900 straight to 2247.

BTC is up 7%, while ETH is up 18%—ETH is outperforming BTC by more than double.

Why?

First, the mean-reversion / rebound effect.
Over the past two weeks, while BTC was ranging sideways between 62,000 and 65,000, ETH was falling harder—dropping from 2,100 to 1,850, a decline of over 11%, while BTC only fell about 3% in the same period. If ETH is oversold, the rebound will naturally be more elastic. It’s math, not a miracle.

Second, the SEC’s new rules directly benefit ETH.
The “Regulation Crypto Asset” framework proposed by the SEC is essentially a green light for financing for tokens that are not securities. ETH has previously faced SEC questions about whether it counts as a security. If this new rule takes effect, that uncertainty is removed. Lower regulatory uncertainty = valuation correction/repair.

Third—and the easiest to overlook—ETH futures positioning structure.
Before the crash, the share of open interest held by ETH futures shorts had already hit a nearly three-month high. A big part of today’s 18% surge is shorts covering, pushing it up. Within 24 hours, the amount of ETH shorts covering exceeded $800 million.

So ETH’s rebound = the triple overlap of oversold recovery + regulatory tailwinds + short covering.

But keep in mind: the ETH/BTC ratio today moved from 0.029 to 0.032. If BTC can’t hold steady above 68,000, ETH’s rebound won’t be able to sustain.

Brothers who have been losing despite being in contracts for more than a year: don’t fixate on chasing returns. The real foundation is learning how to survive through volatility.
Liquidations aren’t terrifying; what’s scary is falling and not correcting your mistakes.
Back then, I started with 1,500U. I also fantasized about doubling overnight. But after two liquidations, my mindset finally collapsed.
I want to tell you the pitfalls I stepped on and the lessons I summarized along the way—so friends who are still exploring can hear it. This isn’t bragging; it’s just hoping everyone takes fewer detours.​​
Real profitability never comes from the windfall gains of a single trade.
I used to think about fast in and fast out to make big money—until my account shrank enough for me to realize that holding positions steadily is far more difficult and valuable than chasing quick profits.
The first change I made was to strictly cap my stop loss for every trade at within 3% of principal.
With a 1,500U account, I can lose at most 45U each time. It may seem slow, but it transformed me from “betting on luck” into “having rules.”​​
What you’re competing on in contracts isn’t guessing the direction—it’s execution.
Now every operation I do follows three bottom lines:
Don’t go against the trend; if the direction is unclear, stay out of the market.
Never enter with full position—at most use 20% of your position.
If you make a mistake, don’t hold on to it to “average down”; once the stop-loss signal triggers, exit immediately.
With just these three rules, after five months of adjustment, I slowly turned from losses into profits.​​
Profit is never “given” by the market—it’s “earned” through risk control.
Many people watch the chart and wait for opportunities, but I care more about controlling risk.
Before every time the market swings violently, I set stop loss and take profit in advance. When price reaches them, I close—if it doesn’t, I wait. No greed, no panic.
This “mechanical” persistence is what makes profits accumulate little by little.
From 1,500U to 18,000U, the hardest part is keeping a steady mindset.
When the market surges, I want to add to my position; when it drops hard, I want to bottom pick. And every time that happens, I force myself to close the software and rest.
This small habit helps me avoid at least four possible liquidations. Turns out, in the market, staying steady matters more than anything.

Trump threatens to escalate military action against Iran, but the market responds with a surge—BTC is up 10.90% in 24 hours.

In theory, this is a classic geopolitical risk: diplomatic room is squeezed and the regional situation heats up. What’s interesting, though, is that the crypto market not only didn’t fall—it rallied across the board. - Short term: Geopolitical conflict escalates → safe-haven demand rises → BTC is treated like “digital gold” and sees aggressive accumulation; this +10.90% move is the proof. Also, if Iran faces tighter sanctions, demand for crypto as local capital flows out increases as well—double buying.
- Medium term: As long as it remains a situation of “bluster but no real fighting,” risk appetite won’t be destroyed. Only when real fighting starts will the logic switch; the historical script of “down first, then up” (based on past regional conflicts) will likely repeat.

Clearly bullish. ETH leads the majors with +19.16% over 24 hours, suggesting that capital isn’t just buying BTC as a hedge—it’s also betting on upside volatility and playing catch-up. #termmax @termmax  Borrowing and lending on-chain often makes interest feel like a “post hoc hindsight”—only after your funds are transferred does the system tell you the exact cost. But what if the price of capital were laid out on the table for everyone to choose before the trade is executed? That’s a completely different business logic.

Honestly, at first I treated TermMax as just a plainly visible fixed-interest borrowing platform. It wasn’t until I closely examined their 2026 whitepaper that I realized the underlying logic runs much deeper. The most ingenious part is that it slices assets into two relatively independent components: FT and XT. In simple terms, they dismantle a single, bulky debt into two pieces. FT functions like a zero-coupon bond that settles at maturity; XT represents the time cost and the liquidity premium. If you need to pull funds back midway, you can sell your XT for cash at any time. This approach turns the creditor’s claim into tradable instruments that can be independently priced.

What truly flipped my perspective was the rollout of the V2 version. Now the order book has fully aligned with Limit Orders. The lending side can lock in a minimum return threshold, while the borrowing side can cap their maximum cost. Immediately after that, the system’s underlying Order Aggregator compiles quotes from different participants and matches them. At this stage, interest is no longer the kind of “dead data” where you just take whatever the pool offers—it becomes market parameters forged by real competition between buyers and sellers.

Based on this momentum, TermMax is already stepping, halfway at least, into the threshold of the on-chain interest rate market, even though it’s still too early to call it an “interest rate exchange.” That said, the biggest obstacle for this model is always trading depth. Having orders on the book doesn’t necessarily mean prices are fair. If there aren’t many participants in the market, the yields posted on the order book are just air castles—once large capital moves in, prices will break through.

In the coming cycles, I’ll focus relentlessly on several key metrics. First, whether both short- and long-term capital can produce a credible yield curve. Second, whether real long-versus-short battles in the limit-order pools are genuinely active. Finally, I must closely track how much slippage the actual borrowing costs incur after those whales hit the market with large orders. #eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  在链上搞借贷，利息往往是个“事后诸葛亮”——只有当你的钱划转出去，系统才会告诉你确切的成本是多少。但假如资金的价码，能在交易落锤前就摆上台面任人挑选呢？这就完全是另一套商业逻辑了。

坦白讲，起初我只把 TermMax 当成个随处可见的固定息借贷平台。直到我细扣了他们 2026 年的那份白皮书，才发觉里面的底层逻辑大有乾坤。最精妙的一笔，就是把资产切割成了 FT 和 XT 两个相对独立的部分。简单来说，他们把一笔原本沉甸甸的债务直接解体了：FT 的角色相当于到期刚兑的零息债券；而 XT 则代表了时间成本和流动性溢价。如果中途急需回笼资金，你随时能把手里的 XT 抛售套现。这种做法，直接让债权变成了可以各自独立标价的交易品种。

真正让我彻底扭转偏见的，是 V2 版本的铺开。现在的盘口全面接轨了 Limit Order（限价单）。放水的一方可以咬死一个最低回报底线，拿钱的一方也能定死自己的最高成本上限。紧接着，系统底层的 Order Aggregator 会把各路神仙的报价汇总到一起撮合。走到这一步，利息再也不是那种“池子给多少你就吃多少”的死数据，而是买卖双方真刀真枪拼杀出来的市场参数。

按这个势头看，TermMax 半只脚已经踏进了链上利率市场的门槛，尽管现在管它叫“利率交易所”还为时过早。但说句实在话，这类模式最大的拦路虎永远是交易深度。要知道，盘口上有单子，绝不代表价格是公允的。要是市场里没几个人玩，那些挂在上面的收益率纯粹就是空中楼阁，大资金一砸就穿。

接下来的周期里，我会死磕它几个核心指标：首先是看长短期的资金能不能跑出一条靠谱的收益率曲线；其次是看限价池里的多空交锋是不是真的活跃；最后必须盯紧那些巨鲸砸出大单后，真实的借贷成本到底会产生多大滑点。#eth $ETH

特朗普表示，任何允许其金融机构、企业、机场或政府实体向伊朗提供支持的国家，都将面临“巨大的经济后果”。他要求立即停止石油走私、货币互换、现金转移、船舶注册和利用空壳公司等活动，并呼吁美国盟友与美国一道孤立伊朗。特朗普再次表示，“伊朗永远不会拥有核武器”。

美国财政部周三宣布，计划将长期名义息票国债的流动性支持回购操作规模至少提高一倍，从每次操作最多20亿美元提升至至少40亿美元。此次调整覆盖10年至20年期以及20年至30年期国债领域，将于2026年9月9日生效，并持续至2026年11月4日。
【美联储纪要“鹰声”不小：许多官员保留加息选项】

【AI生物科技股Twist Bioscience涨超22%】
合成生物学公司Twist Bioscience周三涨22.64%，并带动部分AI概念生物科技股走强。此前Anthropic披露，其利用Claude Opus 4.8和Mythos Preview针对15个靶点开展蛋白质设计实验，并选择Twist Bioscience和Adaptyv Bio作为外部独立评估机构，负责实际生产并测试AI设计的蛋白质。

#termmax @termmax  To be frank, TermMax’s so-called “explosive growth” results from all the promotions they’ve been pushing lately left me utterly unmoved. In this line of work for long enough, you get immune to these superficial tricks. Instead of those fancy, hollow numbers, I obsess over one very real metric: when this new-hot-issue frenzy dies down, how much capital will truly be willing to stay locked in their agreements?

A few days ago, they teamed up with a Binance wallet for a joint promotion. They set up five check-in thresholds—clearly trying to scoop up a round of heads through social shares, then hoping to grab conversions along the way. But the problem is the timing: the event went live on August 17, and right on the heels of that—August 25—is the highly anticipated TGE.

This kind of rushed schedule is basically handing opportunists a knife, blowing up the market’s “sweep the fur” sentiment to the max. How many of these bounty-chasing mercenary farmers are genuinely here to experience the product? Most of them are just passing through, showing up for a check-in.

What feels even more surreal is the data fighting on both ends. On-chain metrics are as revealing as the BTC in our wallets—no room for faking.

Official claim: they boast they secured 1.5 million addresses, 90,000 daily active users, and the funds in the pool amount to as much as 90 million USD.

Third-party data: the monitoring platform directly calls them out—reported funds are only 31.28 million, and in the past 30 days they even fled 7.1%.

The two stories are worlds apart. Even if all that “millions of exposure” is real people, if in the end they can’t back it with cold hard cash, and they just use a bunch of dead-end task progress to look good, what’s the difference from self-deception?

In marketing circles, the best at inflating bubbles is this: heat up the scene, and fill up the interactions. But the moment expectations are met and the subsequent airdrops stop, these “mercenaries” will run faster than anyone—straight into thin air.

So, August 25 is the real make-or-break exam—the moment where it’s truly sink or swim. When that day arrives, I want to see how many new wallets actually stay and hold. Lock both the money and the people into the product—that’s when you truly know they have skills. If the moment the wind shifts they show their real face, then all the initial hype was nothing but a blood-loss purchase.

After their TGE lands, what percentage of real capital do you think they can keep for retention? #eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  坦白讲，TermMax 最近铺天盖地宣发的那份“爆发式增长”成绩单，我看完内心毫无波澜。在咱们这行待久了，对这种表面功夫早就免疫了。比起那些虚头巴脑的数字，我更死磕一个极其现实的指标：等这波打新热潮平息，到底还有多大体量的资金，甘愿沉淀在他们的协议里？

前几天他们搭着 Binance 钱包搞了波联合活动，整出 5 个打卡门槛，摆明了是想靠社交转发先捞一波人头，再指望顺手牵羊做转化。但问题就出在这个节奏上：活动 8月17日 匆匆上线，紧贴着 8月25日 就是万众瞩目的 TGE。

这种火急火燎的时间表，简直就是给投机客们递刀子，把市场的薅毛情绪直接拉爆。这批盯着奖励冲锋的羊毛党，有几个是真心奔着体验产品去的？绝大多数不过是来走个过场、签个到罢了。

更让人觉得魔幻的，是两头打架的数据。链上指标跟咱们钱包里的 BTC 一样，是底裤，容不得半点造假。

官方口径： 吹嘘自己拿下了 150万 个地址、9万 日活，池子里的资金高达 9000万 美金。

第三方数据： 监控平台直接打脸，账面资金仅仅只有 3128万，过去 30 天甚至还跑路了 7.1%。

两边的说法差了十万八千里。就算你这百万级别的曝光都是真人，如果最后兜不住真金白银，光拿一堆死号的任务进度来充门面，跟自欺欺人有什么区别？

圈内搞营销，最擅长的就是吹泡泡：把场子搞热，把交互刷满。可一旦预期兑现、后续的空投停发，这帮“雇佣兵”绝对跑得比谁都快，直接作鸟兽散。

所以，8月25日 才是真正刺刀见红的大考。等那天到来，我倒要看看，还有多少新钱包会做留存。能把钱和人都焊死在产品里，才算有两把刷子；要是风声一过就原形毕露，前期砸的热度纯粹是一笔血亏买卖。

你觉得这波 TGE 落地之后，他们到底能稳住百分之几的真实资金留存率？#eth $ETH

Russian forces launched a large-scale airstrike on Kyiv; 12 people were killed, yet BTC rose to $69,576. Why hasn’t the geopolitical conflict moved the market this time?

The Russia-Ukraine conflict has escalated again. In the short term, sentiment is negative, but BTC actually jumped 8% in 24h.

Russia launched a large-scale attack on Kyiv, killing at least 12 people. The market is worried about two things: first, the West may further increase military support for Ukraine, escalating the intensity of the conflict; second, a geopolitical risk premium may rise, prompting traditional capital to seek safety. But to be honest, the crypto market’s reaction this time is a bit unusual. BTC is quoted at $69,576, up 8.07% in 24 hours; ETH is up even more—16.95%—completely treating the war as if it doesn’t matter.

Market impact
Let’s make the transmission path clear: geopolitical conflict → gold and U.S. Treasuries rise → risk assets are theoretically pressured → BTC should, in principle, fall in tandem. But this time it didn’t follow that script, suggesting that the market’s pricing main driver isn’t there right now. Funds are paying more attention to liquidity expectations. Ironically, the escalation of the conflict strengthens the bargaining logic that “the more chaotic the situation, the sooner the rate cuts.”

- Short term: sentiment is somewhat bearish, but it’s being offset by liquidity expectations. BTC will likely churn in a high range. If $69,576 doesn’t break down, there’s no real basis for a rush of risk-off selling pressure. The extreme case is if the conflict spills over into the NATO level—then that would be the real negative.
- Medium term: increased military aid means global military spending and fiscal expenditures keep swelling. In the long run, hidden inflation stickiness is actually an implicit drag on risk assets.

My take
I’m neutral and watching. BTC’s 8% gain shows bullish sentiment is still there, and the geopolitical negative hasn’t broken through the buy-side. That in itself is a relatively strong signal. But chasing the rally is risky—an escalation can bring a second wave of shocks to the news flow at any time. ETH’s 16.95% one-day surge near $2,246 has already priced in a lot of emotion. The key is whether BTC can hold the $69,000 level. If it holds, the conflict is just noise; if it doesn’t, the “hedging” logic will come back to strike. The risk is that weekend liquidity is thin—any rumor or headline shift could amplify volatility.

One-sentence translation: War news is bearish, but the market is more concerned about whether money will get looser, so it hasn’t fallen for now.

🎯 Expected impact
- Coins: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Neutral (bearish sentiment offset by liquidity expectations)
- Time horizon: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

俄军大规模空袭基辅12人遇难，BTC却在$69,576：地缘冲突这次怎么不动了

俄乌冲突再度升级，短期情绪利空，但BTC反而24h涨8%。

俄罗斯对基辅发动大规模攻击，至少12人遇难。市场担心的是两点：一是西方可能加码对乌军事援助，冲突烈度上升；二是地缘风险溢价抬升，传统资金避险。但说实话，这次加密市场反应有点反常，BTC报$69,576，24h涨8.07%，ETH更是涨了16.95%，完全没把战争当回事。

对市场的影响
传导路径要说清楚：地缘冲突→黄金和美债涨→风险资产理论上承压→BTC按理跟跌。但这次没走这个剧本，说明当下市场的定价主线不在这，资金更关注流动性预期，冲突升级反而强化了“局势越乱、降息越早”的博弈逻辑。

- 短期：情绪面偏空但被流动性预期对冲，BTC大概率高位震荡，$69,576不破位就谈不上避险抛压。极端情况是冲突外溢到北约层面，那才是真利空。
- 中期：军援加码意味着全球军费和财政开支继续膨胀，长期通胀黏性对风险资产其实是隐性压制。

我的判断
这波我持中性观望态度。BTC 8%的涨幅说明多头情绪还在，地缘利空没有击穿买盘，这本身是个偏强信号。但追高风险不小——冲突升级随时可能有第二轮消息面冲击，$2,246附近的ETH单日16.95%的涨幅已经透支了不少情绪。关键看BTC能否守住$69,000一线，守住了冲突就只是噪音，守不住那避险逻辑会回来补刀。风险点在于周末流动性薄，消息面一有风吹草动波动会被放大。

一句话翻译：战争消息是利空，但现在的市场更关心钱会不会更宽松，所以暂时没跌。

- 方向：中性（情绪利空被流动性预期对冲）

​💡 Smart Trading: How to Protect Your Profits in Meme Coin Markets and High Volatility?
We’ve recently seen fast, sudden moves across many cryptocurrencies. Trading and making profits in this market isn’t hard, but protecting your profits is the real challenge for every trader!
Here are 3 essential rules I always apply to reduce risk:
​1️⃣ The Gradual Profit-Taking Rule:
When the trade reaches its first target, don’t wait for the final target with all your liquidity. Take a portion of your profits to ensure real gains.
​2️⃣ Raise Your Stop-Loss (Trailing Stop Loss):
As soon as the price moves in your favor, immediately raise the stop-loss order to your entry price. This way, the trade becomes completely risk-free (Risk-Free).
​3️⃣ Stay Away from Emotions (FOMO):
Entering after a big bullish green candle increases your risk. Always wait for a retest, key levels, and strong supports.
Share in the comments: What strategy do you always rely on to protect your capital? 👇

​💡 التداول الذكي: كيف تحمي أرباحك في سوق الميم والتقلبات العالية؟
​شهدنا مؤخراً تحركات سريعة ومفاجئة في العديد من العملات الرقمية. التداول والربح في هذا السوق ليس صعباً، ولكن الحفاظ على الأرباح هو التحدي الحقيقي لكل متداول!
​إليك 3 قواعد أساسية أطبقها دائماً للحد من المخاطر:
​1️⃣ قاعدة حجز الأرباح التدريجي:
عند تحقيق الصفقة لهدفها الأول، لا تنتظر الهدف النهائي بكامل السيولة. خذ جزءاً من أرباحك لضمان كسب حقيقي.
​2️⃣ رفع وقف الخسارة (Trailing Stop Loss):
بمجرد تحرك السعر في اتجاهك الصاعد، قم برفع أمر وقف الخسارة إلى سعر الدخول فوراً. بهذه الطريقة أصبحت الصفقة خالية تماماً من المخاطرة (Risk-Free).
​3️⃣ الابتعاد عن المشاعر (FOMO):
الدخول بعد شمعة خضراء اندفاعية كبيرة يرفع نسبة المخاطرة. انتظر دائماً إعادة الاختبار والمناطق المفصلية والدعوم القوية.
